title: POC weekly status + regression hunt with Verdant Homes
next_steps: Redwood to run the 10 failing prompt cases through v2 quantized model and share diffs by 2025-02-14
Verdant to provide additional 50 edge-case prompts and expected labels by 2025-02-18
Schedule throughput benchmark with Dedicated config w/ 4xA100 on 2025-02-20
action_items: Samir Rao - reproduce regression locally and attach logs - 2025-02-13
Priya Kapoor - upload edge case prompt set to shared drive + add acceptance criteria - 2025-02-18
Alex Martinez - send updated pricing worksheet and pilot runbook - 2025-02-14
summary: Weekly POC sync focusing on quality regressions observed in prompt set A. Team triaged candidate causes (quantization artifacts, tokenization mismatches, prompt formatting). Action items assigned: Redwood SE to reproduce and capture logs, Verdant to surface more edge prompts, and both to run targeted benchmark on Dedicated capacity. Compliance question re: retention clarified; next legal doc request noted.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we have about 45 minutes — quick check-in on the pilot regressions.
[00:06] Priya (Verdant PM): Yep thanks, sorry for the slight delay, had a standing meeting run over.
[00:12] Samir (Redwood SE): no worries. we've pulled the logs from last night's run, there are about 10 cases that moved from pass to fail after the quantized rollout.
[00:20] Miguel (Verdant Eng): yeah, these are weird — some of the outputs are truncating mid-sentence and others hallucinate numbers.
[00:28] Alex (Redwood AE): right, to confirm, the pilot switched from the FP16 baseline to the 4-bit quantized shard last Wednesday, correct?
[00:35] Samir (Redwood SE): correct — we rolled the q4_0 profile to match your cost target. i suspect two buckets: one tokenization mismatch in the prompt prefixes, and second kernel precision causing logits shift on low-frequency tokens.
[00:50] Leah (Verdant Compliance): quick compliance note — are we still keeping raw transcripts for 90 days? we need the retention window in writing for our audit.
[00:55] Alex (Redwood AE): yes, Redwood default for pilot is 90 days but we can produce a retention statement; i'll add that to the runbook.
[01:02] Priya: ok good. on the prompt side, i uploaded a small set earlier labeled PROMPT-A-v1; some of those have examples where we intentionally format bullet lists — maybe that interacts poorly with prefix caching?
[01:15] Samir: possible. i saw evidence of prefix cache hits in the logs but the decoded tokens looked off. also there's a case where the model seems to switch to Spanish mid-response — likely tokenization ambiguity.
[01:28] Miguel: i can share the exact payloads — they include a customer name with accents, maybe that triggers the language switch.
[01:35] Alex: yeah non-ascii often surfaces when quantization alters marginal token probs.
[01:42] Priya: curious — do you have an easy way for us to test with the FP16 baseline side-by-side? we want to show product folks the delta.
[01:50] Samir: we can run a 100-case diff job — will take a few hours. i'll prioritize the 10 failing examples first to get quick feedback.
[01:58] Priya: perfect.
[02:02] 
[02:15] Speaker 2: (overlap) hey — we also got a ping from legal about SSO attributes, they want assurance that RBAC map won't leak firmware... um wait, sorry that was garbled.
[02:26] Leah: basically we need to confirm SAML assertion attributes can be scoped to groups, and audit logs show user actions by email.
[02:34] Alex: yes, Redwood supports SAML with group scoping and audit trails — i'll share the security pack after.
[02:40] Miguel: back to regressions, is there a quick mitigation? we need to keep the pilot running without rolling back to FP16 if possible.
[02:48] Samir: short-term mitigation: increase sampling temperature to reduce overconfident low-prob tokens? probably won't help truncation. alternate: pin model to FP16 for the two problematic routes while keeping quantized elsewhere.
[02:59] Priya: can we route by policy? like keep the cheap quantized for property-descriptions but FP16 for contract text.
[03:08] Alex: absolutely — our smart routing can operate by endpoint route or by prompt tag. we can configure A/B split for the pilot so some requests go to FP16.
[03:18] Miguel: how fast can you change that? we need it today ideally.
[03:22] Samir: i can put a canary rule in within the hour, but will need the route identifiers from your side.
[03:29] Priya: route ids are in the runbook under /routes/prod-ish — i can paste after.
[03:36] Priya: (paste) route: verdant-property-desc, and contract-summary route is verdant-contracts.
[03:44] Samir: great, i'll set verdant-contracts to FP16 and leave property-desc on q4 for now.
[03:50] 
[04:03] Alex: let's walk the failing cases quickly — Miguel, can you read one?
[04:07] Miguel: sure — Case 7: prompt asks to summarize inspection notes, expected: a bulleted list of 5 items, got: one sentence then '...' and then it outputs phone number random digits.
[04:20] Samir: saw that — the model injected an index number token sequence that looks like it's sampling from unconstrained numeric token space; likely post-tokenizer alignment issue.
[04:30] Priya: Case 3 had a special char — 'Å' — and output started answering in Portuguese.
[04:36] Samir: yeah tokenization wedge. i'll add normalization in the preprocessor as a short-term fix (normalize unicode to NFKC) and re-run.
[04:47] Miguel: ok.
[04:52] 
[05:05] Alex: on scoring, has your evaluation harness changed? last week we saw threshold drift on our automated pass/fail metrics.
[05:12] Priya: we updated the scorer to weigh coverage higher, maybe that changed pass/fail. but drift aligns timewise with quantized rollout which is why we suspected inference change.
[05:23] Samir: to be safe, we'll run both model variants through the scorer so we can attribute delta to model vs scorer change.
[05:33] Priya: that would be helpful.
[05:36] 
[05:50] Speaker 1: (soft) can we also check guardrails — a few false positives flagged when contract clauses included 'non-compete' mentioning competitor names. the guardrails flagged them as PII leakage.
[06:02] Leah: yes compliance saw that — we need tuning to avoid overblocking legal text.
[06:08] Samir: we'll adjust the regex and ML filter thresholds for the guardrail; also provide a whitelist override for contracts route.
[06:17] Priya: perfect.
[06:20] 
[06:32] Alex: ok next, dataset — Priya you mentioned adding 50 edge prompts?
[06:38] Priya: yes we'll put together a supplemental set focused on accented names, long bullet lists, nested lists, and numerics. will include expected labels.
[06:47] Miguel: also i'll export raw token logs for the 10 failing runs and drop them in the shared folder.
[06:54] Samir: that's great — token logs will let us inspect token indices around truncation.
[07:00] 
[07:12] Alex: timing: Samir will reproduce and attach logs by Thursday 2/13, i will send pricing and retention language by Friday 2/14, and we target a dedicated throughput bench on 2/20 — does that align?
[07:26] Priya: yes that's good.
[07:29] Leah: legal will need the SOC2 overview and the retention note in writing — please cc our legal alias.
[07:37] Alex: will do.
[07:40] 
[07:55] Miguel: one question — in the Dedicated bench can you simulate our average concurrency of 120 req/sec with median sequence length of 320 tokens? we need p95 latency under 400ms.
[08:06] Samir: yes we can simulate that workload; we'll include KV cache warmup patterns and realistic arrival distribution. we'll share the bench config prior to run.
[08:16] Priya: if p95 goes above 400ms what's the mitigation?
[08:20] Alex: options: add more GPUs, enable more aggressive batching tradeoffs, or route some traffic to lower-cost regions with looser p95 goals. we'll document the tradeoffs.
[08:31] 
[08:45] Alex: any other items?
[08:48] Priya: none here.
[08:50] Leah: just to confirm, guardrail whitelist for contracts and retention email to legal.
[08:55] Alex: confirmed. i'll follow up with notes and the runbook link.
[09:02] Samir: i'll post logs and the repro steps in the ticket.
[09:07] Priya: thanks everyone.
[09:10] Alex: thanks — we'll send notes and next steps. bye.
[09:14] (call ended)
